acceptance_criteria.statement: ExecuteApprovedProposal remains one deep application call. Pre-acquisition current Workspace/resource authorization, ExecutionAuthorizer, exact compatibility and m4r1 verification may fail fast but grant no dispatch authority. A denial creates no execution and makes zero provider calls.

acquire_execution uses fresh PostgreSQL clock_timestamp after blocking locks and atomically creates the sole generation-1 owner, database-time lease, executing state, immutable authorized binding snapshot and audit. Concurrent losers make zero provider calls.

One Workspace-scoped dispatch_authority_epoch serializes every supported mutable Workspace/resource/execution authorization, exact capability/binding/policy selector and reference-key change. Sources outside this protocol cannot authorize M4 dispatch.

After acquisition, one private PostgreSQL authorize_and_issue_dispatch transaction locks execution then authority epoch, reloads and evaluates all current authority/reference/compatibility facts, samples fresh database time, verifies owner/generation/deadline, and atomically persists one opaque m4-dispatch-v2 permit plus audit. It accepts no caller assertions and has no mutable-authority gap.

m4-dispatch-v2 binds exact Workspace, proposal, logical execution ID, stored fingerprint, capability/binding/policy/reference digests, authority epoch/witness, owner, generation, database times, purpose and signing key. It is integrity-protected, privately constructed, read-back-idempotent and the only create_ticket envelope.

The SQLite reference provider verifies the permit and exact request, acquires BEGIN IMMEDIATE with zero mutation, then a private PostgreSQL receipt guard locks execution and authority epoch and samples fresh clock_timestamp after locks. It admits only the exact current permit/epoch/owner/generation/binding before deadline and retains those locks until the bounded SQLite effect plus idempotency outcome is durable.

Provider admission is totally ordered with later revocation and Issue #78 takeover without provider/process wall clocks. Post-deadline receipt, fencing, epoch mismatch or guard loss creates zero SQLite rows. Admission before deadline may finish its already-admitted bounded commit once; provider state/idempotency remains SQLite-owned and independent from ToolActionStore.

Observation/finalization require current generation-1 owner and fresh PostgreSQL-time lease. SQLite atomically commits ticket or one closed rejection with idempotency outcome; same fingerprint replays, different fingerprint conflicts, before-commit rolls back and after-commit acknowledgement loss remains one durable outcome.

Only direct success and target_not_found, validation_rejected or policy_rejected finalize. Receipt-possible outcomes and proof-no-write rejection remain executing/202 with provider-first recovery required; fingerprint conflict remains executing/409 with no retry authority.

Append-only audit reconstructs execution actor, both current decisions, exact compatibility, authority epoch/witness, database-time lease/permit, provider identity, immutable intent, observations and outcome without secrets or raw provider identifiers; M1-M3 regressions remain green.

design_decisions.decision: WriteProposalWorkflow.handle remains the only application-facing write workflow Interface. Dispatch authorization, authority epoch, permit and provider receipt admission are internal seams hidden by ExecuteApprovedProposal.

Permit issuance is linearized with current authority and exact compatibility in one PostgreSQL transaction under one Workspace authority epoch. A revocation either commits first and denies issuance or commits after an exact witnessed permit.

The deterministic reference provider uses a PostgreSQL receipt guard and fresh post-lock clock_timestamp while retaining the database fence through its short local SQLite commit. This is preferred over a bounded provider-clock assumption for M4 release evidence.

Receipt admission before deadline is the provider-acceptance linearization point. Guard failure before SQLite durability rolls back with proof no write; a future arbitrary remote vendor needs a separately approved time/dispatch protocol.
Issue #77 owns only generation-1 acquire, dispatch, receipt admission and fencing. Issue #78 owns provider-first reconciliation, takeover, generation 2+, retry authority and stale-owner recovery.

invariants: No provider dispatch without one current authority/compatibility decision atomically bound to one stored permit under the current Workspace authority epoch.
No SQLite ticket or idempotency mutation occurs before a fresh PostgreSQL receipt admission, and the PostgreSQL fence remains held through SQLite durability.
Application and provider wall clocks never decide lease or receipt validity; fresh PostgreSQL clock_timestamp after blocking locks is authoritative.
Logical execution identity and request fingerprint are server-derived, immutable and reused unchanged.
Provider effect and idempotency outcome commit atomically or both roll back; ToolActionStore never invents provider truth.
The capability registry remains static and typed; no plugin framework, model/system approval, generation-2 fixture or reconciliation workflow is introduced.
Raw provider IDs, routing handles, permit keys/MAC bytes and authority secrets never enter public or audit projections.
out_of_scope: ReconcileExecution, stale-lease takeover, generation 2+, write-retry authorization and post-takeover stale-owner recovery, owned by Issue #78.
An arbitrary remote vendor protocol, distributed transaction or bounded provider-clock contract; SQLite plus PostgreSQL is the deterministic M4 release boundary.
Dynamic plugins, capability discovery or a general plugin framework.
Editing immutable proposals or reusing approval after material capability, binding or policy change.
Final Milestone 4 fixed-point code review, which remains forbidden until Issues #75-#79 complete.

test_cases.statement: After AcquireApplied, independently change Workspace/resource/execution authority, capability/binding/policy selector and reference-key state before authorize_and_issue_dispatch.
test_cases.oracle: The transaction observes each change, stores no permit, makes zero gateway calls and remains executing/202 with sanitized before_provider_receive.

test_cases.statement: Race an epoch-advancing revocation against permit issuance while dispatch authorization holds its canonical locks; also race concurrent same-generation issuers.
test_cases.oracle: Revocation-first denies or issuance-first records the exact prior epoch. No permit is stale at issuance, and at most one canonical permit/audit exists for the generation.

test_cases.statement: Freeze/skew application and provider clocks, delay a valid permit past its PostgreSQL deadline, and block admission lock acquisition across expiry.
test_cases.oracle: Fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time rejects before SQLite mutation; a transaction-start timestamp cannot revive expired authority and all non-PostgreSQL clock skew is irrelevant.

test_cases.statement: Pause at sqlite_writer_locked_before_postgres_admission and postgres_admitted_before_sqlite_commit while racing an epoch mutation or fenced generation change.
test_cases.oracle: SQLite has zero mutation before admission. After admission, competing changes cannot commit until the terminal SQLite outcome is durable; no overlapping old-generation first write exists.

test_cases.statement: Lose the PostgreSQL guard session after admission but before SQLite durability; separately let a healthy admitted request cross its deadline before commit.
test_cases.oracle: Guard loss rolls back ticket and ledger with proof no write. The already-admitted healthy request may commit exactly once and remains idempotent.

test_cases.statement: Forge, cross-bind, corrupt and replay m4-dispatch-v2, and attempt client logical-ID/fingerprint/authority fields.
test_cases.oracle: Only the private server-derived exact envelope is accepted. Every invalid claim produces zero SQLite mutation and no secret/raw identifier exposure.

test_cases.statement: Race acquisition and run concurrent/repeated SQLite writes with before_atomic_commit and after_atomic_commit_before_ack faults.
test_cases.oracle: One generation-1 acquisition and one logical external outcome exist; effect plus ledger both roll back or persist, same fingerprint replays and different fingerprint conflicts.

test_cases.statement: Exercise success, each closed failure, receipt-possible faults, proof-no-write admission rejection and fingerprint conflict through application and HTTP seams.
test_cases.oracle: Only closed outcomes finalize; all non-terminal 202/409 lifecycle, audit and retry-prohibition mappings are exact.

test_cases.statement: Restart/reload PostgreSQL and SQLite independently after direct, indeterminate and conflict outcomes.
test_cases.oracle: Lease, permit, epoch/audit and provider ledger reconstruct independently; provider truth survives Knora restart without raw provider IDs or key material.

test_cases.statement: Run focused M4.3, full pytest, Ruff, Compose and clean Alembic verification.
test_cases.oracle: All exact-candidate checks and M1-M3 regressions are green on the subject SHA.

command_projections.statement: Clean PostgreSQL recreation and Alembic upgrade with pinned runtime.
Focused #77 and full repository pytest with worktree-pinned PYTHONPATH.
Ruff and Docker Compose configuration verification.

required_evidence.statement: Authority-epoch mutation/issuance traces, exact permit witness/digest and zero-call denial counts.
PostgreSQL post-lock time, acquisition/permit/admission lock ordering, delayed receipt, guard loss and zero-SQLite-mutation evidence under clock skew.
Atomic SQLite ticket/rejection plus idempotency rows, fault injection, replay/conflict and independent restart evidence.
Sanitized terminal, indeterminate, pre-receive, admission-rejection and fingerprint-conflict application/HTTP matrix.
Exact subject SHA, focused/full totals, Ruff/Compose exits, clean Alembic head and clean status.

Use one atomic transaction and commit fault tests.

prior_findings.problem: Provider dispatch was not owner/generation/deadline fenced.
prior_findings.required_change: Add database-authorized permit and provider validation.

prior_findings.problem: Database-time authority lacked a deterministic oracle.
prior_findings.required_change: Skew application time and prove database-time decisions.

prior_findings.problem: The last authority check and permit issuance had a mutable change window.
prior_findings.required_change: Linearize all current decisions with permit issuance and test revocation at that barrier.

prior_findings.problem: Provider deadline validation lacked authoritative time ordering under provider clock skew.
prior_findings.required_change: Anchor receipt to fresh PostgreSQL post-lock time and prove post-deadline delivery creates zero SQLite writes.
